It also supports application-level monitoring by tagging queries with business-logic context (for example, model, view, controller, route, user, or host) and offers client/IP-related execution-time insights within documented limitations, and it is documented as generally available as of 2025-02-14.
e6e796cb42170b7a3f4a6e6c84a58953474c986a.evidence_summary: The AlloyDB documentation pages describe what advanced query insights does and how it works, while the release notes provide lifecycle status and GA timing for the feature.

5af36b636fa3c1ae15287623fe74553106f93ba2.extended_definition: For AlloyDB, outbound connectivity for Private Service Connect is the capability to allow an AlloyDB instance to initiate connections to resources in a consumer project via a Private Service Connect network attachment. The docs state that to enable this, you must create a network attachment in the consumer project’s VPC, and that these consumer networks create and manage the PSC network attachments. Evidence also notes a limitation: outbound connectivity cannot be enabled on AlloyDB instances created before March 1, 2025.
5af36b636fa3c1ae15287623fe74553106f93ba2.evidence_summary: The referenced AlloyDB Private Service Connect overview page provides the enabling mechanism (consumer-managed PSC network attachments) and a key availability constraint tied to instance creation date for outbound connectivity.

fae858bec481917e44c6128d9f39807508d7ddc2.extended_definition: The AlloyDB index advisor is a feature in AlloyDB for PostgreSQL that provides index recommendations, including recommendations for creating indexes. It is documented as part of query insights usage, with support for enabling vector search index recommendations (for ScaNN indexes) through the advisor.
fae858bec481917e44c6128d9f39807508d7ddc2.evidence_summary: The cited AlloyDB documentation pages confirm the feature’s function as an index recommendation tool tied to query insights, including ScaNN vector index recommendation support, but do not independently verify GA status or launch-date details in the provided excerpts.

a75ee05e9e6fdec9c421eb2c453ea4a938658d22.extended_definition: AlloyDB cross-region replication is a feature that allows a primary cluster to replicate data and resources to secondary clusters in other regions, and as documented in the AlloyDB release notes, this setup now supports up to five secondary regions. The same release notes also state that cross-region replication supports performing a switchover with zero data loss, which is positioned for disaster-recovery testing and workload migration.
a75ee05e9e6fdec9c421eb2c453ea4a938658d22.evidence_summary: The AlloyDB release notes provide direct evidence for both the five-secondary-region replication limit and the availability of zero-data-loss switchover in cross-region replication for DR or migration use cases.

92c07cc94feec9651ae268ae25f36f6a32120ef4.extended_definition: AlloyDB database performance snapshot reports is a feature (GA as of December 5, 2024) that provides performance reports comparing system metrics between two snapshots taken at different points in time. These reports include metric-based analysis such as wait events and a SQL report section that lists the top 50 queries by total elapsed time, read I/O, and standard deviation of elapsed time to help identify performance issues. Coverage for specific wait events is documented in the report reference, indicating what can be analyzed in the snapshots.
92c07cc94feec9651ae268ae25f36f6a32120ef4.evidence_summary: The release notes confirm GA availability, scope, and SQL-report details for AlloyDB performance snapshot reports, while the reference page documents the supported wait-event metrics within those reports.

83f032dd2d600e69a8d938f1727e63fa04d2f212.extended_definition: AlloyDB System insights is a unified AlloyDB monitoring dashboard for PostgreSQL instances that provides a customizable database monitoring experience in a single view. It includes predefined metrics and other Google Cloud metrics, and AlloyDB monitoring can also be done via either this AlloyDB System Insights dashboard or the Cloud Monitoring dashboard.
83f032dd2d600e69a8d938f1727e63fa04d2f212.evidence_summary: The AlloyDB release notes explicitly describe the feature’s introduction and capabilities, stating it is a unified, customizable dashboard with predefined and Google Cloud metrics, and that AlloyDB instances can be monitored through AlloyDB System Insights or Cloud Monitoring.

510d097fe9664f87a6960913f8b8d83579279cc5.extended_definition: AlloyDB for PostgreSQL supports provisioning a new AlloyDB cluster from a backup of Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL. The AlloyDB release notes state that clusters can be set up using a copy of a Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL backup, including free-trial cluster setup, and later describe migration from Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL to AlloyDB using that backup as GA. This is a backup-based cluster provisioning path from an external source backup into AlloyDB.
510d097fe9664f87a6960913f8b8d83579279cc5.evidence_summary: The release notes provide direct dated announcements that AlloyDB cluster creation/provisioning from Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL backups was introduced and later available as GA migration support.

c00e902e0a1a96939a66a3af4cf527696fe32513.extended_definition: Model endpoint management in AlloyDB and AlloyDB Omni is an AlloyDB AI capability that lets users maintain a per-project registry of AI model endpoints from different sources or providers. In AlloyDB AI use cases, it is used to register and call remote AI models, and the Vertex AI integration guidance includes workflow steps that lead to calling remote model endpoints. The provided release-note text also links this feature to AlloyDB AI functionality (including AI operators/query features), but the excerpts describe it as a preview-capability in the versions cited.
c00e902e0a1a96939a66a3af4cf527696fe32513.evidence_summary: The release notes document model endpoint management as a key AlloyDB AI feature with a per-project model endpoint registry, while AI use-case and Vertex AI integration pages provide evidence of using it to register and call remote models.

a47bac04fc8e43359009bc69ee50162bdbcb1d65.extended_definition: AlloyDB cluster storage capacity defines the maximum database storage allowed per AlloyDB cluster, with the documented quota announced in release notes. The documented limits are at least 64 TiB per cluster in all locations (April 29, 2024) and later 128 TiB per cluster in all regions where AlloyDB is available (April 09, 2025).
a47bac04fc8e43359009bc69ee50162bdbcb1d65.evidence_summary: The AlloyDB release notes provide explicit dated feature entries for cluster storage quota increases to 64 TiB and then 128 TiB per cluster.

6ee7c236ec6f64d40b94e314b95d0c959b70c1ab.extended_definition: AlloyDB in-place major version upgrade is a managed operation that upgrades the PostgreSQL major version of an existing AlloyDB cluster without replacing the cluster in place. According to AlloyDB release notes, the feature supports upgrading a cluster from PostgreSQL 14 or 15 to PostgreSQL 16, and it progressed from Preview (reported 2024-10-28) to General Availability (reported 2025-03-19).
6ee7c236ec6f64d40b94e314b95d0c959b70c1ab.evidence_summary: The cited release-notes page is the authoritative source confirming both availability milestones and the supported source/target versions for AlloyDB in-place major version upgrades.

180f6809227e9c42efedc5efd89fbd6f40feded8.extended_definition: AlloyDB for PostgreSQL supports creating AlloyDB clusters with PostgreSQL 16 compatibility, and these release notes also state that AlloyDB clusters can be created using PostgreSQL 16. In a later release note update, Google Cloud documents that the default major PostgreSQL compatibility for new AlloyDB clusters is PostgreSQL 16 (effective May 14, 2025).
180f6809227e9c42efedc5efd89fbd6f40feded8.evidence_summary: The cited AlloyDB release notes provide direct evidence that PostgreSQL 16 compatibility is supported for new AlloyDB clusters and was later set as the default major version.

c958de87f44ede3d21c08202e09c4914f823c051.extended_definition: Database Migration Service supports a homogeneous migration path from PostgreSQL to AlloyDB for PostgreSQL version 16, meaning PostgreSQL source databases can be migrated to AlloyDB while retaining the same database engine family. The release notes also indicate DMS is used to migrate databases to AlloyDB, with explicit added support for this AlloyDB 16 destination.
c958de87f44ede3d21c08202e09c4914f823c051.evidence_summary: The AlloyDB release notes page explicitly states that Database Migration Service supports homogeneous PostgreSQL-to-AlloyDB migrations and specifically notes added support for AlloyDB for PostgreSQL version 16.

3b0efed0b5629ccc94e5b03ebf447a06e6350ca6.extended_definition: AlloyDB free trial clusters are an AlloyDB feature documented in the release notes that allows creating trial clusters (including from a copy of a Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL backup), and which reached general availability before being announced as available in all AlloyDB regions. As of November 15, 2024, the release notes state that these free trial clusters are available in all regions. Trial-duration and storage-limit details are not shown in the provided snippets, so those specifics are not confirmed from this evidence alone.
3b0efed0b5629ccc94e5b03ebf447a06e6350ca6.evidence_summary: The release notes excerpts provide rollout milestones (GA and all-regions availability) and one documented setup method for AlloyDB free trial clusters.

bffa8870f25e6a005669ed3ca67a92e20fa31ed2.extended_definition: The alloydb_scann extension is an AlloyDB for PostgreSQL extension that implements an efficient nearest-neighbor index powered by the ScaNN algorithm for vector search use cases. The feature is used alongside the vector extension and, according to the ScaNN reference, requires both `vector` and `alloydb scann` to be installed before creating a ScaNN index; the AI documentation also notes support for PostgreSQL 14, 15, 16, and 17.
bffa8870f25e6a005669ed3ca67a92e20fa31ed2.evidence_summary: These pages confirm alloydb scann’s role in AlloyDB vector workflows, its ScaNN-based nearest-neighbor indexing behavior, supported PostgreSQL versions, and the requirement to install both extensions before using ScaNN indexing.

4b29df9c1361d444104a64587abc7e4af9ffdd3f.extended_definition: AlloyDB free trial clusters can be created using a copy of a Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL backup, enabling trial cluster setup directly from that backup source. The AlloyDB for PostgreSQL release notes state this capability was added on September 25, 2024, and also indicate broader rollout milestones (GA in July 2024 and availability in all regions by November 2024).
4b29df9c1361d444104a64587abc7e4af9ffdd3f.evidence_summary: The cited AlloyDB release-notes page provides the feature announcement and rollout timing confirming backup-based free trial cluster creation from Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL backups.

It is an assistive query-performance diagnostics capability that helps detect, troubleshoot, and prevent database and query performance problems in near real time by improving query visibility, and later release notes indicate active queries and advanced query insights reached general availability in 2025. The feature’s observability model includes tagging/attributing queries by business-logic and stack context (such as model, view, route, user, and host) and captures high-impact client addresses when client IP tracking is enabled.
a890299c8685324adbab0cf77657383a749520ba.evidence_summary: The release notes establish preview/GA timing for Enhanced Query Insights and active queries, while the overview page defines Query Insights’ monitoring purpose, tagging/traceability approach, and a documented capture limitation.

a0a1a2580a6f4cde56f54414eca4a1bef5050f1e.extended_definition: In AlloyDB for PostgreSQL, this feature means that when a database cluster is created, the admin password secret supplied at creation is kept instead of being removed afterward. 07f36e6c4293b9b2ea01be7877c18dad9da58307.extended_definition: AlloyDB now supports organization policies backed by custom constraints, allowing administrators to define and apply policy rules to AlloyDB resources such as instances, clusters, and backups. fd5aee91e40f6a6d4e509cfbdc5e90eaca7cb34a.extended_definition: Public IP support for AlloyDB allows an AlloyDB instance to be configured with a public IP address so it can accept connections from authorized external IP addresses. The feature is enabled during instance setup (for example with the `--assign-inbound-public-ip` option or by enabling Public IP in the UI) and access can be restricted with external network CIDR authorization. Google released this support as generally available on July 22, 2024, with outbound public IP connectivity on primary and secondary instances also noted as GA on September 30, 2024.
fd5aee91e40f6a6d4e509cfbdc5e90eaca7cb34a.evidence_summary: The release notes confirm GA dates for public IP capabilities, and the instance creation guide provides operational details on enabling public IP and authorizing external network access.

550f3bf6d1a8ae6a4ee49d5eefc5a66631734b26.evidence_summary: The release notes and AI documentation together establish that model endpoint management is in preview, describe it as a per-project model endpoint registry, and show how registered endpoints are consumed inside AlloyDB through SQL-based AI capabilities.

0cb73fe74d1735d31817df285241b611b6eee8b3.extended_definition: AlloyDB Private Service Connect is a feature of AlloyDB for PostgreSQL that allows an AlloyDB instance/cluster to be accessed from multiple VPC networks, including networks from different groups, teams, projects, or organizations. It is configured through the AlloyDB cluster API via a `pscEnabled` option (with a default to enabled when neither `pscEnabled` nor an explicit network field is provided), and access is governed through a service connection policy that authorizes the PSC connection between AlloyDB and consumer VPC networks. Release notes state this feature is generally available (GA), with outbound connectivity for PSC-enabled clusters also marked GA.
0cb73fe74d1735d31817df285241b611b6eee8b3.evidence_summary: The AlloyDB overview page defines PSC’s cross-VPC connectivity purpose, the API reference defines how PSC is enabled and defaults at cluster creation, and the release notes confirm GA availability and related PSC endpoint behavior.

d037c475c0f2f0f81d310896745991c9a36cb697.extended_definition: AlloyDB supports setting maintenance windows for clusters so that non-emergency maintenance is scheduled only during a specified weekly period. This lets users control when planned maintenance can run rather than allowing it at arbitrary times. Release-note text also states that clusters that have not received that release may use self-service maintenance for updates.
d037c475c0f2f0f81d310896745991c9a36cb697.evidence_summary: The AlloyDB release notes introduce the maintenance window feature and explicitly state that configured weekly windows limit non-emergency maintenance events to those periods.

It combines an Explorer pane with an enhanced query editor so users can browse, query, and modify database content from a single interface. The feature was documented as generally available in April 2024.
4232acf1bf5343148fb1da521d8b3b14bf45cefc.evidence_summary: The AlloyDB quickstart confirms console access flow (sign-in and Studio navigation), while release notes define AlloyDB Studio’s GA status and core capabilities (authorized in-console SQL access, query execution, and Explorer plus enhanced query editor for browsing/querying/modifying data).

ee13cab1f0b14a0f1b92d7cabfbc07ec14ac83cd.extended_definition: Database Center is an AlloyDB feature (within Gemini in Databases) described as an AI-assisted dashboard that gives a single centralized view across the entire AlloyDB database fleet. Release notes also state that AlloyDB integrates with Database Center to provide prioritized health monitoring in the Google Cloud console, indicating its role in fleet operations and health management.
ee13cab1f0b14a0f1b92d7cabfbc07ec14ac83cd.evidence_summary: The AlloyDB release notes explicitly introduce Database Center as an AI-assisted, centralized fleet-view dashboard and later confirm its integration for prioritized health monitoring in Google Cloud console.

e77ab324a0958208f06cb3c0bd8cf967360336a6.evidence_summary: The index advisor flags page documents the advisor’s supported controls and recommendation behaviors, while the release notes describe it as a fully managed advisor that tracks regular workload queries and generates index recommendations (including ScaNN vector recommendations).

984387f54938794f20aa190c566eb01b1d6072ea.extended_definition: Continuous backup and recovery in AlloyDB is a cluster-level backup mode that enables point-in-time recovery within an adjustable retention window. It is configured on a cluster via `gcloud alloydb clusters update` using the continuous backup recovery window parameter, and can be disabled with `--no-enable-continuous-backup`; the feature defines how far back in time you can restore from continuous backups. After enabling, Google documents that it may take up to 24 hours to complete configuration and activate the continuous recovery capability.
984387f54938794f20aa190c566eb01b1d6072ea.evidence_summary: The release notes confirm rollout milestones, while the backup configuration and overview pages document what the feature does, how it supports point-in-time recovery, and how it is enabled or disabled.

05d970efb0d0e8af319615450c163d3471b95c5d.extended_definition: Chat API now supports retrieving and updating a user's notification settings for a Chat space; Adds Chat API methods to get and update a user's space notification settings.

afabb9edd35ff9d49407f0f45c12b2f69e1c3455.extended_definition: Chat apps can now respond to quick commands selected by users from the message reply area in a Chat space.

35448f8f259f26fdd58677cb7c8384b66cee668f.extended_definition: Chat API now supports mentioning users who are not in a space or are in an import-mode space when sending messages with user authentication.

a69d1a98684b97d73ed4436d0e7f8f162575283b.extended_definition: Chat apps can create announcement spaces in Chat API using app authentication.

1bccec3cb5bd025e59c79af872b09c92545bc1b1.extended_definition: Chat apps can now create, update, and retrieve space permission settings through Chat API methods using app authentication.

261215cc72b84c2bfcd6c40ad3af37e7480ec706.extended_definition: In App Engine flexible environment, updated health checks refer to the default use of split health checks for applications, where liveness checks verify the VM and container are running and health check behavior can be customized via app.yaml. Google documentation says these split health checks are enabled by default, and it points to a dedicated migration guide for moving to split health checks.
261215cc72b84c2bfcd6c40ad3af37e7480ec706.evidence_summary: The referenced App Engine flexible environment page provides evidence that split health checks are the default mode and that behavior is customizable through app.yaml, with a pointer to a migration guide for the split-health-checks transition.

5f4c3e9198c0000840ae2c7bae8b8dbcf75178b1.extended_definition: OBJ.GET_READ_URL is a BigQuery SQL function that returns a STRUCT for a Cloud Storage object containing a read URL and a status value (and related URL/access metadata as shown in examples). The 2026-03-31 release notes describe this as returning that STRUCT and note that image results can be rendered in the BigQuery Cloud console. This enables workflows to use the generated read URL in downstream SQL/Python processing to access object data.
5f4c3e9198c0000840ae2c7bae8b8dbcf75178b1.evidence_summary: The release notes confirm the behavior change and console rendering, the function reference defines the return type/fields at a high level, and the multimodal tutorial demonstrates the actual STRUCT output shape containing access URLs with a read URL key.

bfb00e31a4ca2baefb396f94fceff2f50c269fb7.extended_definition: BigQuery SEARCH INDEX creation supports column-level granularity configuration through `CREATE SEARCH INDEX`, including a `default index column granularity` for the index and an `index granularity` option per indexed column. These settings determine how much column information is stored for each indexed column, and the per-column setting can override the index default. Google Cloud release notes describe this as a feature that can further optimize search query performance.
bfb00e31a4ca2baefb396f94fceff2f50c269fb7.evidence_summary: The DDL reference documents the supported search index granularity options and override behavior, while the release notes confirm that setting column granularity during search index creation is an introduced feature aimed at improving query performance.

f5289ea6ce41a4e2085d511e17871f686b240ec1.extended_definition: BigQuery’s OBJ.MAKE_REF function has a behavior where it automatically retrieves the latest metadata for a referenced Cloud Storage object and writes that metadata into the ref.details field. The feature describes automatic metadata enrichment of the reference object record rather than requiring a separate explicit metadata fetch step.
f5289ea6ce41a4e2085d511e17871f686b240ec1.evidence_summary: The BigQuery release notes explicitly confirm automatic latest Cloud Storage metadata population into ref.details for OBJ.MAKE_REF, while the multimodal tutorial shows practical usage contexts where OBJ.MAKE_REF and object metadata fields are exercised.

5afadcad3d66ec23b64b9fabd8b4316a04eefa5d.extended_definition: BigQuery’s GoogleSQL supports Cloud resource connection management through Data Definition Language statements: CREATE CONNECTION, ALTER CONNECTION ... SET OPTIONS, and DROP CONNECTION. The CREATE syntax supports optional project and location scoping ( [[project.]location.]connection_id ) and options such as friendly name and description; ALTER CONNECTION SET OPTIONS is used to update connection properties, and DROP CONNECTION removes the named connection. According to BigQuery release notes, this DDL-based management capability was introduced on April 2, 2026.
5afadcad3d66ec23b64b9fabd8b4316a04eefa5d.evidence_summary: The BigQuery DDL reference provides statement-level syntax and usage examples for CREATE/ALTER/DROP CONNECTION, while the release notes explicitly date the feature launch to April 2, 2026.

d0ad102684f0210c01e93d546bc6edc54f3d966c.extended_definition: BigQuery ObjectRef support was updated to allow ObjectRef functions to run using either direct access mode or delegated access mode, as stated in the March 31, 2026 BigQuery release notes. In practice, ObjectRef usage is tied to object reference operations (including GCS objects) and is controlled through ObjectRef-specific IAM permissions, including read and write actions on ObjectRefs granted at the connection scope. The exact technical distinction between direct and delegated access behavior is not described in the provided excerpts beyond the stated support for both modes.
d0ad102684f0210c01e93d546bc6edc54f3d966c.evidence_summary: The release notes provide the feature declaration for direct vs delegated ObjectRef access, while the tutorial and IAM documentation provide supporting context on ObjectRef usage patterns and required BigQuery ObjectRef read/write permissions.

3ba0a1c236db045809d3530ecc97c579d9ee62e4.extended_definition: AI.DETECT_ANOMALIES (also shown as ML.DETECT_ANOMALIES in examples) is a BigQuery function used to perform anomaly detection on time-series input data using BigQuery ML forecasting models such as TimesFM, ARIMAX, and multivariate ARIMAX variants. In documented usage, it returns anomaly flags and score columns (for example: is anomaly, lower bound, upper bound, and anomaly probability) and accepts option settings like anomaly probability threshold via a STRUCT argument. The provided excerpts do not explicitly mention a custom context_window parameter or controlling the number of recent data points, so support for that specific aspect cannot be confirmed from these pages alone.
3ba0a1c236db045809d3530ecc97c579d9ee62e4.evidence_summary: These BigQuery tutorial pages demonstrate the AI/ML.DETECT_ANOMALIES API for time-series anomaly detection and its supported options and output fields, but they do not provide direct evidence of a configurable context_window/custom context control.

c2847362ae8afdc0844b7462e7759b10617b3af2.extended_definition: In BigQuery, AI.FORECAST now supports a "latest timestamp" parameter that defines the latest timestamp value used as the starting point for a forecast. This parameter allows callers to base generated forecast values on history up to a specified timestamp rather than only using an implicit endpoint.
c2847362ae8afdc0844b7462e7759b10617b3af2.evidence_summary: The release notes explicitly announce that AI.FORECAST supports specifying the latest timestamp for forecasting, while the linked ARIMA PLUS tutorial page provides adjacent AI time-series forecasting context but does not add explicit syntax for this specific parameter.

9eb264ff5bf361c4342998ed902d8f6150a40a02.extended_definition: BigQuery supports creating non-incremental materialized views over Spanner data, which are intended to improve query performance by periodically caching results. In BigQuery DDL, these views are created with `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW`, and the `allow non incremental definition` option (default `false`) enables a broader set of SQL query definitions for materialized view creation.
9eb264ff5bf361c4342998ed902d8f6150a40a02.evidence_summary: The release notes explicitly announce non-incremental materialized views over Spanner data for periodic result caching, while the DDL reference documents the `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW` syntax and the `allow non incremental definition` option that controls support for expanded materialized view query definitions.

af4d7d60837044b935f3a9e8ef0688a1b86055e0.extended_definition: AI.EVALUATE in BigQuery is used to evaluate forecast outputs against a reference time series based on historical data. The BigQuery release notes state that AI.EVALUATE supports a custom context window that controls how many of the most recent data points are used by the model; evidence for MASE specifically being returned as an output is not explicit in the provided excerpts.
af4d7d60837044b935f3a9e8ef0688a1b86055e0.evidence_summary: The release notes provide direct evidence of AI.EVALUATE usage and custom context-window support, while the tutorials confirm EVALUATE-based forecast evaluation and output reporting but do not explicitly show MASE in the cited snippets.

b319578259386500d5365dfbdbb71004df850cb9.extended_definition: BigQuery supports reverse ETL to Cloud Spanner by allowing `EXPORT DATA` statements that use a BigQuery Cloud resource connection. This feature, announced in the March 26, 2026 release, uses Cloud resource connections as the mechanism to authorize BigQuery's write-out/export path to Spanner. In BigQuery, a Cloud resource connection is a defined BigQuery object backed by a service account for access to other Google Cloud resources.
b319578259386500d5365dfbdbb71004df850cb9.evidence_summary: The release notes directly state the feature (connection-based `EXPORT DATA` reverse ETL to Spanner), while the SQL reference and tutorial pages provide supporting evidence of Cloud resource connection concepts and creation mechanics.

2b8860ba35b0c4cc2efe3f5aba5dd6a41afd0034.extended_definition: AI.EMBED is a BigQuery built-in function used in SQL generation expressions to generate embeddings from input data. BigQuery release notes indicate it became generally available on March 23, 2026 for creating embeddings from text or image data, and documentation shows it works with Vertex AI embedding models, with embeddings represented as ARRAY<FLOAT64> values (or STRUCT<result ARRAY<FLOAT64>, status STRING> in preview autonomous embedding generation workflows).
2b8860ba35b0c4cc2efe3f5aba5dd6a41afd0034.evidence_summary: The three official BigQuery pages confirm AI.EMBED’s purpose, GA scope, input support, model backing, and how its generated vector outputs are represented in schema-related usage.

b4432f2c6d9b475e721a2a2d9bb040b9c15176e8.extended_definition: BigQuery query execution graph visualization is a job-level troubleshooting feature that presents a visual map of a query’s execution, including execution graph, SQL text, and execution history in the job details performance view. It adds query-text heatmapping to the execution graph so users can identify which SQL text contributes to stages that consume more slot-time and inspect stage-level execution details.
b4432f2c6d9b475e721a2a2d9bb040b9c15176e8.evidence_summary: The release notes confirm the introduction of visual SQL-to-stage mapping for performance debugging, and the admin jobs explorer documentation shows how users access execution graphs, SQL text, and heatmap-driven execution analysis for selected jobs.

bb783b35ba2cf2a8d613381dd8d8cf6c9437e1f7.extended_definition: BigQuery conversational analytics now supports BigQuery ML function calls, specifically AI.FORECAST, AI.DETECT ANOMALIES, and AI.GENERATE. The documented behavior for AI.DETECT ANOMALIES includes use with BigQuery ML’s built-in TimesFM model in conversational analytics, including support for a custom context window.
bb783b35ba2cf2a8d613381dd8d8cf6c9437e1f7.evidence_summary: The release notes provide the feature-level announcement and function list, and the TimesFM anomaly tutorial provides concrete usage evidence for AI.DETECT_ANOMALIES within BigQuery ML.

4f3840fe7d875f104e98b1e9766e069a57cbb0e6.extended_definition: The provided Google Cloud documentation confirms that BigQuery supports creating and managing partitioned tables (including setting default partition settings and converting sharded tables to partitioned tables) and supports declaring partition columns for external tables via SQL DDL. These capabilities provide the partitioning primitives that can be used by downstream features, but the excerpts do not explicitly document conversational analytics-specific behavior such as partition-aware SQL generation or direct cost/performance optimization.
4f3840fe7d875f104e98b1e9766e069a57cbb0e6.evidence_summary: The cited pages provide evidence of BigQuery partition table features (table creation/management, partition columns, and CLI partition controls) but do not explicitly prove the conversational analytics optimization claims.

730471e54f5c6eb30cbea24e74a04cc952cdb53d.extended_definition: BigQuery data preparation is a Gemini-enabled BigQuery Studio capability that offers context-aware, AI-generated recommendations to transform and cleanse data for analysis. It is exposed as a managed preparation workflow in BigQuery (including scheduling and release concepts), with permissions reflected through roles such as BigQuery Studio User and Gemini for Google Cloud User plus access to the underlying data. 730471e54f5c6eb30cbea24e74a04cc952cdb53d.evidence_summary: The Gemini overview and release notes establish what BigQuery data preparation does and how it is accessed/secured, while none of the provided snippets directly document Cloud Storage or Google Drive file-sourcing for this feature.

b8ae5adc48d803f2e436cfde41640b33e08c6456.extended_definition: BigQuery AI.EMBED is a built-in function that can be used directly with a Vertex AI embedding model endpoint, specifically including `gemini-embedding-001`. The feature supports generating embeddings from input data, and official release notes state that AI.EMBED is available for creating embeddings (including text/image in GA) while docs describe it as generating embeddings via Vertex AI embedding models.
b8ae5adc48d803f2e436cfde41640b33e08c6456.evidence_summary: The release notes confirm direct AI.EMBED use with the `gemini-embedding-001` endpoint and GA availability, while the vector search introduction explains AI.EMBED’s role in generating embeddings through Vertex AI models.

37206ff9ce7540e7dcaf7b067e09a5fa87028e9c.extended_definition: Conversational analytics in BigQuery Studio is an in-editor feature of the BigQuery Studio SQL editor that lets users start conversations and chat with the results of their queries. 37206ff9ce7540e7dcaf7b067e09a5fa87028e9c.evidence_summary: The release notes confirm the feature’s existence and core behavior (chatting with query results in BigQuery Studio’s SQL editor), while the IAM page lists BigQuery Studio roles but does not explicitly document permissions specific to this conversational analytics action.

4baad5a7a6cd5ae10f7d8fdb3055384dec174545.extended_definition: BigQuery supports embedding generation in SQL through the `AI.GENERATE_EMBEDDING` function, including models defined as remote models in BigQuery ML. The documented workflows show creating a remote model (for example from an open-source embedding model) and calling `GENERATE EMBEDDING` in SQL to produce embeddings for text from table columns, with results including embedding vectors (and associated status for each row). For supported model types, the function also applies to structured table data and can be used with multimodal content sources.
4baad5a7a6cd5ae10f7d8fdb3055384dec174545.evidence_summary: These pages document how to create and use remote models in BigQuery ML with `AI.GENERATE_EMBEDDING`, including SQL examples for generating text (and supported multimodal) embeddings from table data and the expected output shape.

298aa83ee9953b2d3c799c01936abb3b515546f2.extended_definition: BigQuery conversational analytics gained support for ObjectRef integration, allowing analysts to reference and work with unstructured Google Cloud Storage objects (including images and PDFs) through ObjectRef functions and ObjectRef/ObjectRefRuntime values. This enables those referenced objects to be included in conversational analysis workflows, with ObjectRef execution supporting both direct and delegated access paths. BigQuery also defines dedicated IAM roles for this capability, including ObjectRef admin and reader roles that grant read/write access to referenced objects.
298aa83ee9953b2d3c799c01936abb3b515546f2.evidence_summary: The release notes confirm the feature launch date and scope for ObjectRef in conversational analytics, the tutorial demonstrates practical image/PDF ObjectRef usage, and IAM documentation defines ObjectRef roles and permissions.

64dca2ba9b63e05eac5517a097982de17fc47114.extended_definition: BigQuery ML supports creating remote models that are backed by models served through Vertex AI via `CREATE MODEL ... REMOTE WITH CONNECTION`, using a Cloud Resource connection to the Vertex AI endpoint. As of the March 06, 2026 release, BigQuery can create remote models using the Vertex AI `gemini-embedding-001` model and open embedding models from Vertex Model Garden or Hugging Face when those models are deployed to Vertex AI. The syntax for remote model configuration includes model-source options such as `VERTEX AI MODEL ID`, `HUGGING FACE MODEL ID`, and `MODEL GARDEN MODEL NAME`, and the model can be used for inference (for example with `ML.PREDICT`).
64dca2ba9b63e05eac5517a097982de17fc47114.evidence_summary: The release notes announce the embedding-related remote model capability and date, while the SQL reference and tutorial provide the remote `CREATE MODEL` configuration surface and prediction usage behavior in BigQuery.

8697fd3347aeee73facb23c0bc09de7edc7ddeca.extended_definition: BigQuery supports vector similarity search through the `VECTOR SEARCH` SQL form, which is used in queries by specifying a vector table, the vector column, and a subquery-based query vector (for example, generated via AI-generated embeddings). When a vector index is used, VECTOR SEARCH applies approximate nearest-neighbor search to improve vector search performance, with the trade-off of reduced recall and more approximate results. The provided excerpts do not explicitly confirm a documented alternate syntax specifically for single-vector queries, so that specific feature distinction is weakly evidenced here.
8697fd3347aeee73facb23c0bc09de7edc7ddeca.evidence_summary: These pages document core VECTOR_SEARCH usage and behavior with vector indexes in BigQuery, but do not clearly describe a separate "alternate" single-vector syntax.

f54a53cf98a19da908ceffbd82d64b5f6236ef5f.extended_definition: This feature exposes BigQuery cross-region replication observability in Cloud Monitoring by publishing metrics for dataset replication latency and network egress bytes. It is intended for BigQuery cross-region replication and managed disaster recovery workflows, enabling operators to monitor these replication health and traffic indicators.
f54a53cf98a19da908ceffbd82d64b5f6236ef5f.evidence_summary: The BigQuery release notes entry dated March 04, 2026 states that dataset replication latency and network egress bytes are now available as Cloud Monitoring metrics for cross-region replication and managed disaster recovery.

a713133bef1c207531fe0a89171e95c0f14fa8eb.extended_definition: BigQuery global queries are controlled by a region-scoped setting that can be enabled (for example, `region-us.enable global queries data access = true`) to allow data access across regions in a query workflow. In this configuration, the feature permits copying/querying data from the configured region in a global query scenario; when set to `FALSE` (the default), global queries cannot copy data from that region regardless of the project where jobs run.
a713133bef1c207531fe0a89171e95c0f14fa8eb.evidence_summary: The referenced BigQuery DDL documentation excerpt defines a `global queries data access` region-level option, gives its default as `FALSE`, and states that disabling it prevents global query data copy operations from that region.

2e26aa6ae9a58b310093b9bce3081881e86aabcc.extended_definition: AI.CLASSIFY is a BigQuery function for classifying text into user-defined categories, and as of February 12, 2026 it supports multi-label classification. This indicates AI.CLASSIFY can return multiple category labels for a single input instead of only one.
2e26aa6ae9a58b310093b9bce3081881e86aabcc.evidence_summary: The BigQuery release notes explicitly add AI.CLASSIFY multi-category (multi-label) support on Feb 12, 2026 and define AI.CLASSIFY as text classification into user-defined categories.

3804e0173521b75b041d5fa5d7327b7451269209.extended_definition: BigQuery’s AI.GENERATE and AI.GENERATE TABLE functions support a custom output schema for structured responses, and the field metadata in that schema can include descriptions. 3804e0173521b75b041d5fa5d7327b7451269209.evidence_summary: The release notes explicitly state that AI.GENERATE and AI.GENERATE TABLE now support field descriptions in custom output schemas, while the tutorial demonstrates how AI.GENERATE TABLE uses output schema mappings to shape model outputs.

2fc916271e4ade440061a0db68b503f182b49950.extended_definition: BigQuery Conversational Analytics is an early-access BigQuery feature that enables working with BigQuery through a conversational analytics agent in a chat-style workflow. The official release notes describe support for custom glossary terms for the agent (including Dataplex Universal Catalog terms), clickable suggested follow-up questions in the Cloud console, and ObjectRef-based integration with Google Cloud Storage for that workflow.
2fc916271e4ade440061a0db68b503f182b49950.evidence_summary: The BigQuery release-notes page confirms the feature exists in early access and lists recent enhancements, but it provides release updates rather than a complete formal product definition.

5d2a7178708a19b631481eaccb6a04a9bea793ad.evidence_summary: These pages define BigQuery SQL named/positional query-parameter syntax and use cases, with release notes adding parameter-related capabilities in the Python client, but none explicitly document Cloud Console Query Editor-specific execution support.

b153ed7ee0e9760c009adde19050bebb7a0cd855.extended_definition: BigQuery Continuous Query is a BigQuery feature with dedicated predefined IAM roles, including the BigQuery Continuous Query Service Agent role (`roles/bigquerycontinuousquery.serviceAgent`), which grants BigQuery Continuous Query access to service accounts in the user project, and a role for service account access to a continuous query. Google Cloud documentation also states that models can be created through the Google Cloud Console user interface via the BigQuery UI workflow for working with models, indicating support for in-console model creation in addition to SQL-based authoring.
f52c699cfc9682b6937fb541358b20b3e810119c.evidence_summary: These pages show that BigQuery ML models are created with `CREATE MODEL` and that the documentation points to a Google Cloud Console UI path for creating models, though detailed UI steps are not fully provided in the excerpts.

ee3edbbdba4eb81328a2f5722098ef7270176c7c.extended_definition: BigQuery supports a predefined data masking rule named RANDOM_HASH that can be specified in a DATA MASKING POLICY as the masking expression for a column. The rule returns a salted hash of the column value and is described as providing stronger security than the standard Hash (SHA-256) masking rule. Google’s release notes indicate this rule was added on January 29, 2026.
ee3edbbdba4eb81328a2f5722098ef7270176c7c.evidence_summary: The release note explicitly introduces RANDOM_HASH as a new predefined masking rule and explains its salted-hash behavior compared with SHA-256, while the DDL reference confirms predefined masking rules are used via masking expressions in DATA MASKING POLICY definitions.

69013e870db48dfb3b3d230cd94bc7a7baaeea51.extended_definition: BigQuery Data Transfer Service supports Shopify as a data source, allowing data to be transferred from Shopify into BigQuery. Google Cloud documentation lists Shopify as a supported (Preview) source in the DTS source catalog and the BigQuery release notes explicitly state that BigQuery Data Transfer Service can now transfer data from Shopify to BigQuery. This transfer is configured as a Data Transfer configuration that can run on a recurring schedule to keep BigQuery updated.

582e6e460d472e618732dbfdd05cd8e76782451b.extended_definition: The BigQuery remote MCP server is a BigQuery feature that provides a remote Model Context Protocol (MCP) endpoint to let LLM agents perform data-related tasks. The BigQuery release notes state this capability was introduced on December 10, 2025, and later note that after March 17, 2026, enabling BigQuery results in the BigQuery MCP server being automatically enabled.
582e6e460d472e618732dbfdd05cd8e76782451b.evidence_summary: The cited release notes directly introduce the BigQuery remote MCP server feature and provide a documented behavioral update about its auto-enable behavior.

0864c335db10bd5c421a2126da3da4061e7c111f.extended_definition: BigQuery’s Gemini Cloud Assist feature provides job-history insights that can explain why specific queries were slow and identify the most resource-intensive queries over the past day. 0864c335db10bd5c421a2126da3da4061e7c111f.evidence_summary: The BigQuery release notes page explicitly describes Gemini Cloud Assist’s job-history insight capability for slow-query and resource-intensive query analysis and notes labeling of assistant-initiated jobs.

6f8cedc7da92b550f509ebca2f212a76a4ecde59.extended_definition: BigQuery’s `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE` and `LOAD DATA` statements support additional loading options for parsing and mapping source files, including a time zone setting, date/time format controls, and null-handling controls. The Jan 6, 2026 release notes state these statements now support `time zone`, `date format`, `datetime format`, `time format`, `timestamp format`, `null markers`, and `source column match` options, allowing users to define how date/time fields are interpreted, how NULLs are recognized, and how input columns map to the table schema. In BigQuery’s SQL and CSV-loading documentation, `null marker` is a string option for NULL representation and `source column match` controls the strategy used to match loaded columns to the schema.
6f8cedc7da92b550f509ebca2f212a76a4ecde59.evidence_summary: The cited pages together confirm the Jan 2026 feature update and provide formal option definitions for `null marker` and `source column match` in BigQuery DDL and CSV load workflows.

Evidence for how to configure this connector via the provided CLI snippets is incomplete, as the shown data-source list examples do not include SQL Server.
5ee1bf772ea6a0eda902613b45b6de3fb24b08d3.evidence_summary: The release notes page directly confirms SQL Server-to-BigQuery transfer support in BigQuery Data Transfer Service (including incremental transfer support), while the bq CLI reference provides surrounding transfer-configuration context but no SQL Server-specific setup details in the excerpt.

The BigQuery docs state it supports embedding generation (explicitly text in the vector search intro), while release notes indicate it can create embeddings from text, image, audio, video, or documents and that text/image embedding generation became generally available (GA) on March 23, 2026; when used in generation expressions, AI.EMBED is the only supported generation-expression syntax and requires a connection id if an endpoint argument is used.
a5473c85337fe93579229609d78d251fe54daf7b.evidence_summary: The intro page establishes AI.EMBED’s purpose for generating embeddings, release notes add supported input modalities and GA milestone details, and the SQL reference documents required usage constraints in generation expressions.

cd79c08ffd2c3b361c26cd55f1e84e0584019dec.extended_definition: BigQuery generative AI support includes creating remote models in BigQuery and invoking them via SQL functions such as AI.GENERATE TEXT and AI.GENERATE EMBEDDING for tasks like sentiment analysis, keyword extraction, and text embedding. The provided tutorials demonstrate this with specific models (for example, gemini-2.5-flash, Gemma, and Qwen text-embedding), but they do not provide evidence that the feature specifically uses a global Vertex AI endpoint or explicitly supports Gemini 3.0.

a44bb25016da11363b11dfe2f17939fc0c13627e.extended_definition: BigQuery ML exposes AI.GENERATE functions to run generative queries in SQL against Vertex AI Gemini models, including AI.GENERATE TEXT for text generation and analysis use cases. It also supports table-valued generation via AI.GENERATE TABLE, which returns structured output from unstructured inputs such as text, images, audio, and video using a provided output schema. In practice, these functions are invoked through a BigQuery remote model/connection to a Gemini endpoint (for example, gemini-2.5-flash) and can produce one-row text outputs or multi-column structured results.
a44bb25016da11363b11dfe2f17939fc0c13627e.evidence_summary: The release notes define the feature scope (AI.GENERATE/ML.GENERATE TEXT support for Gemini, and AI.GENERATE TABLE for structured outputs from unstructured text/images/audio/video), while the tutorials provide concrete usage patterns with a Gemini endpoint and example SQL/DataFrame calls.

caa9931739e9f5b9964a3e857a89852fe107dda9.extended_definition: BigQuery Data Transfer Service (DHTS) supports creating and running transfer configurations to import data from Salesforce into BigQuery using transfer commands such as `bq mk --transfer config` and `bq mk --transfer run`. Google Cloud release notes state that Salesforce was added as a generally available BigQuery Data Transfer Service source, and IAM documentation identifies transfer-specific BigQuery Data Transfer Service permissions/roles used to manage transfers. The provided evidence does not explicitly confirm an incremental (CDC) Salesforce-specific transfer mode.
caa9931739e9f5b9964a3e857a89852fe107dda9.evidence_summary: The release notes confirm Salesforce as a GA BigQuery Data Transfer Service source, the bq CLI page confirms how transfer configurations and runs are created/executed, and the IAM page lists BigQuery Data Transfer Service transfer permissions and related roles.

74abf187d8f4ec345c3354903edc4d76e3d7891b.extended_definition: The feature is the ability to configure default project and dataset context in BigQuery so that unqualified object names can resolve without fully qualifying every identifier. In practice, BigQuery CLI and SQL examples show that when a default project is not configured, callers must specify names as fully qualified project.dataset.table, while defaults can be supplied (for example, via CLI flags like `--project_id` and `--dataset_id`) and overridden as needed.
74abf187d8f4ec345c3354903edc4d76e3d7891b.evidence_summary: These pages document BigQuery’s default-resolution behavior for project/dataset references in SQL and bq CLI commands, but do not directly mention SQLX or pipeline-task-specific default settings.

8f90f0e01826757f572f7df7c6d2462ecfb4e42a.extended_definition: AI.GENERATE_EMBEDDING is a BigQuery ML SQL function used to generate vector embeddings from input data in BigQuery, including text and multimodal content (such as images and video), via remote models. BigQuery release notes state it is the new preferred version of ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING, providing the same embedding-generation functionality with simplified column output names.
8f90f0e01826757f572f7df7c6d2462ecfb4e42a.evidence_summary: The release notes confirm AI.GENERATE_EMBEDDING replaces ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING, while the tutorial and vector search introduction provide concrete usage examples and supported input types/targets for embedding generation in BigQuery ML.

1d71b3eef1ca3e85da9ee9514bb260e3983ec754.extended_definition: BigQuery now supports using custom constraints with Organization Policy on BigQuery dataset resources, allowing organization-level policy controls at a more granular level by targeting specific fields. The cited release note indicates this enables finer-grained dataset governance for supported fields, rather than only coarse dataset-level controls.
1d71b3eef1ca3e85da9ee9514bb260e3983ec754.evidence_summary: The BigQuery release notes explicitly state that custom Organization Policy constraints can be used for more granular, field-level control on BigQuery dataset resources.

6b56f53e04ee75ed239c6f346e695d623516547a.extended_definition: The provided BigQuery release notes confirm that BigQuery supports Apache Iceberg via the BigLake metastore REST catalog, including GA support with BigQuery catalog federation, credential vending, and catalog management, plus features for interoperability and snapshot access. 6b56f53e04ee75ed239c6f346e695d623516547a.evidence_summary: These release notes document Apache Iceberg REST catalog capabilities in BigLake metastore but do not mention Dataform-driven BigLake table provisioning.

7aa4309991e0dd3160d94d081927a1733e76c1b3.extended_definition: AI.DETECT_ANOMALIES is a BigQuery ML SQL function in BigQuery used to detect anomalies in time-series data. Google Cloud documentation shows it can be run with BigQuery ML's built-in TimesFM model by supplying historical and target time-series data, and it can return anomaly indicators, lower/upper bounds, and anomaly probability output. The function is documented as generally available (GA) and supports a custom context window setting that controls how many recent data points are used by the model.
7aa4309991e0dd3160d94d081927a1733e76c1b3.evidence_summary: The tutorial details practical use of AI.DETECT_ANOMALIES with TimesFM on time-series data, the release notes confirm its GA availability and context-window capability, and the syntax reference includes it as a BigQuery ML detection function in model journeys.

bf703376c0d8ca858da911d95d5f99eb240eb2d8.extended_definition: BigQuery can publish data insights to Dataplex Universal Catalog as metadata. 55c21a4118e271da20284410c5c1f768ed09eff6.extended_definition: AI.GENERATE_TEXT is a BigQuery ML SQL function used with remote models (for example, Gemini or Gemma models) to generate text for tasks such as keyword extraction and sentiment analysis. fe6e1dc78e1dbeeeb2a53a12b8645edf415c4788.evidence_summary: The function reference identifies `JSON KEYS` as extracting unique JSON keys, while release notes confirm the feature’s introduction/use in BigQuery.

3b2fbb8fb86d8f04e9eab3c6bfe6d270838fc625.evidence_summary: The release notes explicitly announce Cloud Storage file loading in BigQuery data preparations, while the Gemini overview page defines Data Preparation as an AI-assisted transformation workflow in BigQuery.

a4327025d16af85cda3b9e1b0030e615e27e0034.extended_definition: BigQuery’s reusable default Cloud resource connection feature lets a project define a default connection that BigQuery can use automatically when creating tables or models. The feature is reflected in SQL connection configuration through DDL and options (for example, a `default cloud resource connection` and the ability to use `DEFAULT` in place of an explicit project-scoped connection string), which indicates project-level and SQL-native reuse of a shared connection.
a4327025d16af85cda3b9e1b0030e615e27e0034.evidence_summary: The release notes announce the feature and the DDL/options reference documents how a default Cloud resource connection is defined and referenced in BigQuery SQL workflows.

7c5a3f7c8e1eac6433425c059f8093c53821cde0.extended_definition: BigQuery managed disaster recovery includes a **soft failover** capability. The BigQuery release notes state that BigQuery now supports soft failover for managed DR, and also describe failover-related API fields that let users choose a HARD or SOFT failover mode and expose a soft-failover start time in reservation replication status.
7c5a3f7c8e1eac6433425c059f8093c53821cde0.evidence_summary: The release notes are the primary source confirming managed DR soft-failover support and providing related reservation failover API signals (mode selection and replication-status timing).

01709720bbea85fd36bac6375b5d1fe55cc3feb4.extended_definition: BigQuery ML supports creating remote models from open embedding models in Vertex Model Garden or Hugging Face (deployed to Vertex AI) and running embedding inference against them from SQL. The inference function used is ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING, and Google documentation also states that AI.GENERATE_EMBEDDING is the preferred replacement with the same functionality and simplified output column names.
01709720bbea85fd36bac6375b5d1fe55cc3feb4.evidence_summary: The release notes provide direct feature evidence for remote open-embedding models from Vertex Model Garden/Hugging Face and mention ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING/AI.GENERATE_EMBEDDING, while the BigQuery ML journey reference lists ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING as a model inference function.

17f6a24fe8facca368267b6ee7b8e4a8b231be01.extended_definition: BigQuery ML allows creating a **remote model** that references a model hosted in Vertex AI by using the `CREATE MODEL` workflow with remote model configuration (for example, endpoint/connection-based setup). According to BigQuery release notes, you can create a remote model based on the Vertex AI `gemini-embedding-001` model, and then use it with the `ML.GENERATE EMBEDDING` function to generate embeddings. The tutorial and syntax references together show the supported creation flow for remote models and their use from BigQuery once the model is created in the dataset.
17f6a24fe8facca368267b6ee7b8e4a8b231be01.evidence_summary: The release notes provide direct evidence of BigQuery support for `gemini-embedding-001` remote models and embedding generation, while the tutorial and CREATE MODEL reference document how remote model creation is configured in BigQuery ML.

9a645e21f0d45ced3a6bf2fa6a30d20dfeb77f93.extended_definition: ST_REGIONSTATS is a BigQuery geography function that combines raster data from Google Earth Engine with vector geography data stored in BigQuery to produce regional statistics. It can be used to compute aggregate raster-derived values over geographic regions, such as the mean of a raster band (for example, temperature) for each polygon feature.
9a645e21f0d45ced3a6bf2fa6a30d20dfeb77f93.evidence_summary: The release notes confirm the feature’s announcement and purpose, while the tutorial demonstrates a concrete ST_REGIONSTATS query that merges Earth Engine raster input with BigQuery vector geography to calculate regional averages.

91b909d3da77e670dd43335b82479985dcd3a795.extended_definition: BigQuery resource utilization charts are monitoring views that show operational health and resource usage data (including job and reservation-related metrics such as slot usage) and provide a dashboard for workload observability. The charts are backed by INFORMATION_SCHEMA metrics views and are used to inspect usage at organization, reservation, or project levels. In Google Cloud release history, the feature added more metrics views and chart configuration in preview (Feb 25, 2025) and became generally available on August 11, 2025.
91b909d3da77e670dd43335b82479985dcd3a795.evidence_summary: The admin-resource-charts page defines how the charts are sourced and secured, while the release notes confirm their preview updates and GA availability date.

7dd79e2e37ac1199178165d5ea7b4ce9df2e0871.extended_definition: BigQuery short query optimization is part of the BigQuery advanced runtime feature, which can be enabled for query execution. It dynamically identifies eligible queries that can run as a single stage, lowering latency and slot usage, with eligibility influenced by factors such as predicted data scan size. BigQuery also exposes a query configuration option (`query runtime`) that controls whether the query processor uses the advanced runtime.
7dd79e2e37ac1199178165d5ea7b4ce9df2e0871.evidence_summary: The advanced-runtime guide details short query optimization behavior and timing, the SQL reference shows how advanced runtime is selected via query options, and release notes confirm feature availability and rollout milestones.

1749d03a51af2b1c7f07b10f9d795430a0f7c0a3.extended_definition: BigQuery vector index drift monitoring and rebuild is a DDL feature that lets users check how much indexed table data has drifted since a vector index was created via the VECTOR_INDEX.STATISTICS function, and then rebuild a changed active vector index using ALTER VECTOR INDEX REBUILD. The rebuild operation regenerates the index via an asynchronous shadow-index training and cutover process and is documented as not requiring index downtime. Running ALTER VECTOR INDEX REBUILD requires a BACKGROUND reservation assignment for the project containing the table, and the feature is labeled as Preview.
1749d03a51af2b1c7f07b10f9d795430a0f7c0a3.evidence_summary: The DDL reference provides the operational behavior and requirements of ALTER VECTOR INDEX REBUILD, while the BigQuery release notes confirm the availability of VECTOR_INDEX.STATISTICS for drift and the use of rebuild when table changes warrant it.

df34d9caae6999c6ed96838fb9889a8abb79b3cd.extended_definition: BigQuery metadata curation in the Google Cloud console supports management of data profile scans and data quality scans (introduced as a feature on July 31, 2025). The release notes also state that data quality scan results can be published as Dataplex Universal Catalog metadata, and enabling that publishing for an existing scan requires editing the scan and re-enabling the publishing option.
df34d9caae6999c6ed96838fb9889a8abb79b3cd.evidence_summary: The cited BigQuery release notes page documents the July 31, 2025 launch of scan management in Metadata curation and the June 18, 2025 capability to publish data quality scan results to Dataplex Universal Catalog metadata.

999ed7c47b4fa3738c6b832086e4a0e2e790eee5.extended_definition: The feature introduces preview options for BigQuery’s `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE` and `LOAD DATA` statements when loading CSV data: `null markers` and `source column match`. `null markers` defines the strings that should be interpreted as NULL values in CSV files, while `source column match` controls how loaded source columns are matched to the schema. These options are documented as statement-level options and are specifically identified as preview functionality.
999ed7c47b4fa3738c6b832086e4a0e2e790eee5.evidence_summary: The release notes provide the feature announcement for preview-only `null markers` and `source column match` on `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE`/`LOAD DATA` CSV loading, while the table/DDL pages provide related syntax context and the null-marker meaning in BigQuery documentation.

1b1376f11b3f0d6fe4b2f26464122f163ff07024.extended_definition: In BigQuery Standard SQL, MATCH_RECOGNIZE is an optional sub-clause of the FROM clause that filters and aggregates rows by matching defined row patterns across table data. It uses PATTERN and DEFINE to describe what sequences of rows qualify, and MEASURES (with expressions such as ARRAY_AGG) to output aggregated results for each match, with matching behavior configurable via options like AFTER MATCH SKIP and USE LONGEST MATCH. Official release notes list MATCH_RECOGNIZE as a new feature in 2025 (shown with dates July 22, 2025 and November 05, 2025).
1b1376f11b3f0d6fe4b2f26464122f163ff07024.evidence_summary: The query syntax page defines how MATCH_RECOGNIZE is structured and used in SQL, while the release-notes page confirms its introduction and public availability in 2025.

fc93ba92107ff9b0f95fe7df5a409eb5eb110fb3.extended_definition: BigQuery’s DISTINCT pipe operator is a pipe-syntax feature that lets query pipelines return only distinct rows from a table. In practice, it adds support for a `DISTINCT` stage in a pipe query so duplicate rows are removed in the pipeline output.
fc93ba92107ff9b0f95fe7df5a409eb5eb110fb3.evidence_summary: The BigQuery release notes are the only provided official source that explicitly describes this feature, stating that a DISTINCT operator can now be used in pipe syntax queries to select distinct rows.

68f398edec19146eb8d0ce709c946608d2685114.extended_definition: BigQuery query syntax supports a `WINDOW` clause that defines one or more named windows as reusable window expressions (`named window AS (...)`) for use with analytic functions. A named window is a defined group of rows used by a window function’s `OVER` clause, and named windows can be combined and referenced there. The provided excerpts show this behavior in BigQuery’s query syntax, but do not explicitly include a pipe-syntax-specific example of the same feature.
68f398edec19146eb8d0ce709c946608d2685114.evidence_summary: The Standard SQL query-syntax page documents the `WINDOW` clause and named window usage in `OVER` clauses, while the Legacy SQL page documents BigQuery window/analytic function concepts generally.

a2ca78b0dfbe6b74820399d92f24f3ad870ef1ec.extended_definition: The provided Google Cloud BigQuery documentation indicates that BigQuery ML model creation is performed using the `CREATE MODEL` SQL statement in BigQuery ML, including training model types such as logistic regression and other model options. The docs also describe related setup, required permissions (`bigquery.jobs.create`, `bigquery.models.create`, `bigquery.models.getData`, `bigquery.models.updateData`, `bigquery.models.updateMetadata`), and where model training results can be viewed, but they do not explicitly describe model creation specifically via the Google Cloud Console UI flow.
a2ca78b0dfbe6b74820399d92f24f3ad870ef1ec.evidence_summary: These pages establish SQL-based BigQuery ML model creation with `CREATE MODEL` and required IAM permissions, with limited UI references to viewing training statistics but no explicit confirmation of a console-based model-creation UI feature.

5a37f32cf77a2499074cbc57a643e853148f146c.extended_definition: The BigQuery batch SQL translator is one of BigQuery Migration Service’s SQL translation offerings and is used to migrate SQL scripts in bulk. It is part of BigQuery’s SQL translation services, which automate conversion of SQL queries into GoogleSQL (and other supported SQL dialects), and is listed alongside the interactive SQL translator and SQL translation API. The service is also described in the context of migration from legacy data warehouses and is available only in BigQuery SQL translator processing locations.
5a37f32cf77a2499074cbc57a643e853148f146c.evidence_summary: The cited pages confirm that BigQuery includes a batch SQL translation path for bulk script migration, that it converts queries to GoogleSQL (plus other supported dialects), and that SQL translators are region-bound.

AS (...)` to define common table expressions (CTEs) before a main query. b0b20c8802edb95abe2ca5a920c74b5f884c26f3.extended_definition: BigQuery migration assessment is a BigQuery capability that evaluates migration workflows for moving workloads into BigQuery, and it is officially documented as available for workflows that use Cloudera and Apache Hadoop (announced June 16, 2025). The same release notes context also indicates BigQuery’s migration tooling includes Impala SQL translation options (interactive translator, translation API, and batch translator) that can be used to migrate Cloudera/Apache Hadoop SQL workloads using Impala to GoogleSQL.
b0b20c8802edb95abe2ca5a920c74b5f884c26f3.evidence_summary: The release notes provide direct feature availability evidence for Cloudera/Apache Hadoop migration assessment, while the IAM page confirms BigQuery Migration Service has its own documented permissions model.

b56c5c5946eb28f741fc6db72643ffc7c9f640a1.evidence_summary: The cited DDL page documents metadata side effects of BigQuery rename operations, specifically that associated Data Catalog tags or Dataplex Universal Catalog aspects are deleted, but it does not describe Data Quality scan metadata publication.

e3cd1f7fc5cda5fada7aa711c8bbff731c1c3a74.extended_definition: BigQuery ML supports multivariate time-series forecasting with the `ARIMA PLUS XREG` model type, described as combining linear regression with ARIMA PLUS. In `CREATE MODEL`, this is configured through time-series options including `TIME SERIES ID COL`, which is a model option for time-series models and accepts one or more ID columns so a single model query can address multiple grouped time series.
e3cd1f7fc5cda5fada7aa711c8bbff731c1c3a74.evidence_summary: The syntax reference documents `ARIMA PLUS XREG` and `TIME SERIES ID COL` as supported `CREATE MODEL` options, while the ARIMA tutorials show `TIME SERIES ID COL` being used in `CREATE MODEL` statements to model multiple IDs/time series within one BigQuery ML workflow.

b93186be4c5911891765e48964f5a097bd635f3c.extended_definition: In BigQuery GoogleSQL, `ARRAY_FIRST` (shown as `ARRAY FIRST` in the provided example) is an array function that returns the first element from an array. The cited example demonstrates retrieving first values from array columns in a `SELECT` query, and it states that `ARRAY FIRST` together with `ARRAY LAST` produces an error when the array is empty. The provided excerpt does not include evidence for preview status or launch date.
b93186be4c5911891765e48964f5a097bd635f3c.evidence_summary: The official BigQuery arrays guide excerpt provides usage examples of `ARRAY FIRST` and documents its empty-array error behavior when used with `ARRAY LAST`.

ecc1d5416d7e179fb0cf9a140c2d139a76557124.extended_definition: In GoogleSQL, `ARRAY LAST` returns the last element from an array value in a `SELECT` expression. The BigQuery arrays documentation shows it as the counterpart to `ARRAY FIRST`, and states that calling it on an empty array raises an error because it cannot return a last element.
ecc1d5416d7e179fb0cf9a140c2d139a76557124.evidence_summary: The cited BigQuery arrays page provides direct usage examples and explicit error behavior for `ARRAY LAST`, establishing its purpose and empty-array failure mode.

7c0ace5d11dfb9d0c19112a2c91260468015ece2.extended_definition: The `@@location` system variable in BigQuery SQL allows a query to specify the location in which the query is executed, and it is set in the first statement of the query. BigQuery release notes describe this as a feature that enables running a query in a user-specified location.
7c0ace5d11dfb9d0c19112a2c91260468015ece2.evidence_summary: The locations page documents how to set `@@location` in query execution, and the release notes page records the feature’s introduction with date context.

60cfbf248c90838b18e7f0ebddb304b746dec8b6.extended_definition: BigQuery supports Vertex AI Provisioned Throughput with the AI.GENERATE and ML.GENERATE functions (notably ML.GENERATE TEXT and AI.GENERATE TEXT) for supported Gemini models, enabling more consistent high-throughput request handling for SQL-based AI generation. BigQuery documentation also identifies AI.GENERATE TEXT as the preferred equivalent of ML.GENERATE TEXT, with the same functionality and simplified column output names.
60cfbf248c90838b18e7f0ebddb304b746dec8b6.evidence_summary: The release notes provide the direct feature statement about Vertex AI Provisioned Throughput and throughput benefits, while the BigQuery tutorials confirm active use of AI/ML.GENERATE text functions with remote models in BigQuery SQL.

6905bb9c1db6051298b3c2b8a49bfe1ae328d6e7.extended_definition: BigQuery materialized views now support Apache Iceberg external tables as a source, allowing a materialized view query to reference Iceberg external table data directly without migrating that data into BigQuery-managed storage. This capability was introduced in the June 09, 2025 BigQuery release notes.
6905bb9c1db6051298b3c2b8a49bfe1ae328d6e7.evidence_summary: The BigQuery release notes explicitly record the feature addition that materialized views can reference Apache Iceberg external tables instead of requiring migration to BigQuery-managed storage.

23a41351e19844b9f6ee706302cc5825201d6e60.extended_definition: BigLake tables for Apache Iceberg naming in BigQuery is a terminology update in which the table type previously referred to as “BigQuery tables for Apache Iceberg” is now called “BigLake tables for Apache Iceberg.” This reflects a naming/brand change for the same Apache Iceberg table feature set within BigQuery.
23a41351e19844b9f6ee706302cc5825201d6e60.evidence_summary: The BigQuery release notes explicitly state that “BigQuery tables for Apache Iceberg have been renamed BigLake tables for Apache Iceberg.”

506f1db19d19e48ac7b26a4c3108e9ebe59f2038.extended_definition: BigQuery column metadata indexing is a feature that enables metadata indexing at the column level in BigQuery for both BigQuery native tables and external tables. The provided release-note snippet confirms its availability but does not include details on indexing behavior, use cases, or performance/security implications.
506f1db19d19e48ac7b26a4c3108e9ebe59f2038.evidence_summary: The cited release notes state that BigQuery column metadata indexing is available for both BigQuery tables and external tables, with no further technical specifics in the provided excerpts.

06f7885809ba94645815abe39aa68b8d479c1dca.extended_definition: As of May 29, 2025, BigQuery added support for running Python code defined in BigQuery DataFrames through the `dbt-bigquery` adapter. This feature specifically enables dbt workflows to execute DataFrames-defined Python logic via the adapter, and Google Cloud documentation directs readers to the dedicated "Use BigQuery DataFrames in dbt" guidance for details.
06f7885809ba94645815abe39aa68b8d479c1dca.evidence_summary: The BigQuery release notes explicitly state this new dbt-bigquery capability and link to dedicated dbt + BigQuery DataFrames documentation.

23b4858cfccfa5891eb4b326e12e9e7c429997b7.extended_definition: In BigQuery, the CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE and LOAD DATA statements support preview options for controlling date/time parsing when loading source data: time_zone, date_format, datetime_format, time_format, and timestamp_format. These options are used for CSV and JSON ingestion to apply a default timezone for TIMESTAMP values without explicit zones and to define custom format strings for DATE, DATETIME, TIME, and TIMESTAMP fields.
23b4858cfccfa5891eb4b326e12e9e7c429997b7.evidence_summary: The loading CSV documentation specifies each parsing option and its behavior, while release notes confirm these options are newly supported (in preview) by CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE and LOAD DATA.

2652efea1936a5e5432bd84d7a452053a84ead27.extended_definition: As of June 2, 2025, BigQuery added support for using Cloud Spanner external datasets with authorized views, authorized routines, and Cloud resource connections. This feature enables authorized-access patterns when reading Spanner data in BigQuery through external dataset integration and connection-based access configuration. Google’s quota documentation further indicates that BigQuery dataset access control for authorized entities is quota-limited (for example, up to 2,500 authorized resources per dataset, including authorized views), so authorization at this scope is governed by documented limits.
2652efea1936a5e5432bd84d7a452053a84ead27.evidence_summary: The release notes confirm the Spanner external datasets feature and its authorized views/routines/Cloud resource connections support, while quota documentation provides supporting constraints on authorized-access entries in dataset ACLs.

6d1d98b2338ee8db0e6092ca3717e572d879f498.extended_definition: BigQuery continuous queries are long-lived continuous SQL jobs designed to continuously process incoming data in real time. BigQuery documentation describes them as running continuously for real-time analytics and machine-learning inference, including support for stateful processing via joins and windowing aggregations across rows or time intervals. Google also defines a dedicated IAM surface for this feature, including predefined roles for service agents and service accounts that grant access to continuous query resources.
6d1d98b2338ee8db0e6092ca3717e572d879f498.evidence_summary: The release notes establish what continuous queries do, and the access-control page confirms the feature has its own predefined IAM roles.

64b0821bc0bf39fef0f855de4c9c7ceddf934769.extended_definition: TreeAH is a BigQuery vector index type created with the CREATE VECTOR INDEX statement using OPTIONS (index type = 'TREE AH'), with optional distance and TreeAH-specific options such as normalization type. It uses Google’s ScaNN algorithm for vector search and is optimized for efficient batch processing, handling roughly a few thousand to hundreds of thousands of embeddings per batch. TreeAH indexes can be partitioned via the PARTITION BY clause of CREATE VECTOR INDEX, and this partitioning behavior is referenced as preview-related in the DDL documentation.
64b0821bc0bf39fef0f855de4c9c7ceddf934769.evidence_summary: The release notes confirm TreeAH support, ScaNN usage, batch-processing performance, and partitioning support, while the DDL and vector search pages define the CREATE VECTOR INDEX syntax/behavior and position TreeAH as a ScaNN-based BigQuery vector index technology.
